annotatedSteps.description: Calculation of energy available at the producer level (phytoplankton)
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
By the 10% law only 10% of energy passes to the next level.
Large fish (4th level) = 10 kJ ⇒ small fishes = 100 kJ ⇒ zooplankton = 1000 kJ ⇒ phytoplankton = 1000 × 10 = 1,00,000 kJ.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Correct application of the 10% law backwards, but arithmetic slip: 1000 × 10 = 10,000 kJ, not 1,00,000 kJ.

annotatedSteps.description: Possibility of three more trophic levels and justification
annotatedSteps.studentWork: No. At each trophic level about 90% of the energy is lost, so after three more levels very little usable energy would be left.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly answered 'No' with proper reasoning of energy loss.

annotatedSteps.description: Identifying the level with maximum pesticide and giving the reason (biological magnification)
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Large fish, because pesticides are non-biodegradable and accumulate at each trophic level (biological magnification), so the highest level has the maximum concentration.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly identified large fish and accurately explained biomagnification.

teacherNote: Parts B and C are excellently answered with complete conceptual clarity and appropriate terminology like 'biological magnification'. In Part A, your method and step-by-step logic were entirely correct, but an extra zero was accidentally added when multiplying 1000 by 10 (giving 10,000 kJ, not 1,00,000 kJ).

rubric.point: Part A: Correct calculation / application of 10% law to find energy at producer level (10,000 kJ)
Part B: Stating 'No' with valid justification based on energy loss at successive trophic levels
Part C: Identifying large fish (highest trophic level) and explaining biological magnification
